title.narrative: INDALOPRENEUR CLIMATE-SMART CLEANTECH ENTERPRISRE SUPPORT PROGRAMME (ICCTEP)

description.narrative: The overall purpose of this grant is to support the establishment/Expansion of; Entrepreneurship Training aimed at Students and Staff at THENSA member universities.In partnership with the Technology Innovation Agency (TIA), the Irish Embassy and the Technological Higher Education Network South Africa (THENSA), the South Africa/Ireland Entrepreneurship Programme was implemented in 2019 to address the demand for more entrepreneurial-minded graduates who will contribute to the economy's growth and job creation. During the study visit to Ireland in 2019, which was attended by THENSA’s delegation of staff and students. The following objectives were identified:Developing the ‘Train the Trainer programme’ for lecturers who will train, guide, mentor and provide university students with all the knowledge required to support their entrepreneurial activities and initiatives.Train young entrepreneurs and develop their ideas into implementable start-ups.Developing a Short Learning Programme (SLP) entrepreneurship curriculum aligned to the National Qualifications Framework at (NQF Level 5) to ensure that all students entering university, as well as the unemployed youth, will have the necessary skills, knowledge, and knowhow to develop their ideas into start-ups businesses. The continuation of the SA/Irish Biomedical Cluster (Advanced Manufacturing for Medical Applications). This cluster is a research collaboration between Munster Technological University (MTU) and THENSA. The main deliverable of this study will add to the previously completed desktop study to develop a database of medical implants available through the MTU network and introduce the Centre for Rapid Prototyping Manufacturing (CRPM) products and capabilities to MTU’s extended network to:Identify gaps and opportunities for collaboration (both with CIT and the medical device manufacturers in Ireland);Introduce CRPM’s products for possible commercialisation within the international network;Benchmark and measure the new deliverables against existing Irish industry levels; focus on delivering internationally accepted products; and collaborate with the Irish universities and industry. The positive outcomes of this grant are largely the research partnerships and links that have been established and will be sustained between the Irish and South African higher education sectors.
